claims.statement: Almost all of the patients I see in my practice with Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis have a history of taking antibiotics for acne, and while that doesn't necessarily prove causation in those particular patients, the medical literature is full of studies that now confirm that antibiotic use, particularly in childhood, is a major risk factor for the development of these diseases.
claims.source_note: [[The Microbiome Solution - Chutkan - Ch11 Rewilding Illness]]
claims.evidence_excerpt: Cites the epidemiological literature. Describes acne antibiotics as especially damaging because: they are broad-spectrum, taken for months or years, and highly active against gut bacteria. Aspirations are taken from only a few inches of the small intestine, which may not represent the whole small intestine.

claims.statement: Doctors prescribe more antibiotics when they perceive the patient wants one. A structured set of 10 questions (Table 11-1) can signal that the patient is "not keen on taking an antibiotic unless absolutely necessary" and shift the clinical conversation from automatic prescribing to shared decision-making.
claims.source_note: [[The Microbiome Solution - Chutkan - Ch11 Rewilding Illness]]
claims.evidence_excerpt: Cites studies showing that "doctors are far more likely to prescribe an antibiotic when they perceive that the patient is interested in taking one." claims.statement: An emulsifier such as polysorbate 80 disrupts mucous membranes and, in effect, emulsifies your microbiome too. And sodium benzoate kills fungi that are supposed to be in the microbiome.
claims.evidence_excerpt: General reference to food science and microbiome literature. The mechanism: emulsifiers disrupt the mucus layer that separates gut bacteria from the intestinal epithelium; preservatives intended to kill food-spoilage microorganisms also kill commensal gut microbes.

claims.statement: Modern Westerners have lost roughly a third of their microbial diversity compared to hunter-gatherer and traditional agricultural populations. This loss is driven by processed foods, antibiotics, C-sections, formula feeding, and hyper-sanitized environments.
claims.evidence_excerpt: References studies comparing Hadza hunter-gatherers, rural African populations, and Amerindians in the Venezuelan Amazon to Western populations. Notes that traditional populations consuming high-fiber diets have microbial species not found in any Western gut.
